 This Mfa Filed U/S.173(1) Of Mv Act, Against The
Judgment And Award Dated 09.07.2021 Passed In
Mvc No.7419/2018 On The File Of The Chief Judge, Court
Of Small Causes, Member, Prl. Mact, Bengaluru,
Partly Allowing The Claim Petition For Compensation
And Seeking Enhancement Of Compensation.

This Appeal, Coming On For Hearing, This Day,
Judgment Was Delivered Therein As Under:
Coram: Hon'Ble Dr. Justice Chillakur Sumalatha
 Oral Judgment
Heard Ms.V.Nithya who represents Sri.Prakash.M.H, learned counsel on record for the appellants.

Also heard Sri.Lakshminarasappa who represents Sri.A.M.Venkatesh, learned counsel on record for respondent No.1.
2.
Challenge in this appeal is the order that is rendered by the Principal Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru in MVC No.7419/2018 dated 09.07.2021.

entities.text: Principal Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: As borne by record, as against the claim for Rs.40,00,000/- in total, the Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.27,91,280/- as compensation and attributing contributory negligence of 50% on the part of the deceased Rajesh, directed the respondents herein to pay the appellants a sum of Rs.13,95,640/-.

4. Arguing the matter, Ms.V.Nithya contends that this appeal is filed challenging the findings of the Tribunal that the deceased Rajesh contributed for the accident to occur and such contribution is to the extent of 50%.
Learned counsel states that the deceased Rajesh was not negligent and indeed the accident occurred due to the sole negligence on the part of the driver of the lorry which is involved in the accident.

Learned counsel submits that though sufficient proof was produced establishing the Smt Subhashini vs M/S United India Ins. Co. Ltd on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90893625/
2 negligence on the part of the driver of the lorry, yet the Tribunal gave a finding that the deceased Rajesh also contributed for the accident to occur and that his contribution to an extent of 50%.
NC: 2024:KHC:45480 5.

entities.text: Smt Subhashini vs M/S United India Ins. Co. Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The submission that is made by Sri.Lakshminarasappa representing respondent No.1 on the other hand is that the deceased Rajesh was proceeding on his motor cycle in a rash and negligent manner and at a high speed and he dashed against the rear portion of the lorry which is involved in the accident and thus he died due to the injuries sustained.
Learned counsel also contends that the Tribunal has rightly fastened negligence to an extent of 50% on the part of the decease Rajesh and therefore, the award needs no interference.

6. The version of the appellants is that on 02.12.2018 in the midnight around 12.30 a.m. while the deceased Rajesh (herein after be referred to as 'the deceased' for brevity) was proceeding on his motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-42-R-8164 from Kanakapura side towards Bengaluru and when he reached near Lakshmipura gate, a heavy goods vehicle i.e., lorry bearing registration No.KA-03-C-079 was proceeding NC: 2024:KHC:45480 ahead of the motor cycle of the deceased at a high speed.

Without giving any indication or signal, the driver of the lorry suddenly applied brakes and turned the lorry to right side due to which the deceased who could not observe the lorry stopped because of the focus lights coming from the opposite vehicle, dashed against the rear side of the lorry due to which he sustained severe injuries and succumbed to injuries on the spot.
7. Undisputedly, a case was registered against the driver of the lorry and finally charge sheet was laid.
Charge sheet was laid against the driver of the lorry only.
Respondent No.1-insurance company summoned the investigating officer and examined him as Rw.1.

While Rw.1 was giving evidence,
respondent No.1-insurance company sought to declare the witness as hostile and accordingly, the witness was declared as hostile.
Thereafter Rw.1 was cross examined by respondent No.1- insurance company.
However, the consistent version of Rw.1 is that, after investigation charge sheet was filed NC: 2024:KHC:45480 against the driver of the lorry only.
During the course of cross examination by learned counsel for the appellants, Rw.1 stated that as per the charge sheet the accident occurred due to sole negligence on part of the driver of the lorry.
8. The appellants produced evidence of Pw.2 who is an eye witness to the accident.

The version of Pw.2 as per his evidence is as under:
"I submit that, on 02.12.2018 at about 12.30 a.m., midnight I was proceeding on my motor cycle from Kaggalipura towards Bengaluru City, at the same time I was noticed that one motor cyclist bearing Reg. No. KA-42-R-8164 as proceeding on same direction, ahead of me at the distance of 40 to 50 feet, when we proceed and reached near Lakshmipura Gate, Kanakapura- Benglauru Main Road, Bengaluru South.

At that time the driver of HGV Lorry bearing Reg. No. KA-03-C-79 has proceeding on the same direction i.e. from Kaggalipura towards Bengaluru City, overtook both motor cycles, with heavy high speed in a rash and negligently without observing any traffic rules and regulations and endangering to NC: 2024:KHC:45480 human life,
Smt Subhashini vs M/S United India Ins. Co. Ltd on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90893625/
3 without switching on hazardous lights or giving any signals, suddenly applied the brake and took the vehicle towards right side, due to the barricade on the road, which is maintained by the police, due to this the said motor cyclist was hit the rear side of lorry, because of he could not observe the lorry at midnight. Impact of the accident the deceased wad died on the spot."

entities.text: Subhashini vs M/S United India Ins. Co. Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 9. Thus the evidence of Pw.2 coupled with the evidence of Rw.1 i.e., investigating officer who investigated the case makes it clear that the accident occurred solely due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the lorry only.
Absolutely there is no evidence on record to show that the deceased was negligent in driving his motor cycle.

Respondent No.1 insurance company which took a specific plea that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the deceased,
failed to establish that fact with substantive proof.
But without considering these facts, the Tribunal gave a finding that NC: 2024:KHC:45480 the contributory negligence on the part of the deceased is 50%.
10. In the light of the foregoing discussion, this Court is of the view that such finding is not on merits and in consonance with the evidence produced.
Therefore, this Court holds that the appeal is required to be allowed setting aside the order of the Tribunal fastening contributory negligence to an extent of 50% on the part of the deceased.

Therefore, the appeal is disposed of with the following:
ORDER (i)
The appeal is allowed.

(ii) The order of the Principal Motor Accidents  Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru in MVC No.7419/2018 dated 09.07.2021 to the extent of attributing contributory negligence on the part of the deceased Rajesh is set aside.

entities.text: Principal Motor Accidents  Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: (iii) Thus respondents are at liability to pay entire compensation to the appellants NC: 2024:KHC:45480 which was ordered by the Tribunal along with interest.
(iv) Respondent No.1 is directed to deposit the entire amount within a period of 8(eight) weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
(v) On such deposit, the appellants are permitted to withdraw the entire amount.

Sd/-
(DR.CHILLAKUR SUMALATHA) JUDGE NS
